identity: Journalist and former Canadian pop star
background: Robin Charles Scherbatsky Jr. was born on July 23, 1980, in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, to a Canadian father, Robin Charles Scherbatsky Sr., and an English mother, Genevieve Scherbatsky. She has a younger sister named Katie. Robin had a difficult relationship with her father, who raised her as if she were a boy. As a teenager, she had a brief career as a bubblegum pop singer under the stage name Robin Sparkles, with a hit single 'Let's Go to the Mall'. After a mall tour and a failed attempt to shift to grunge music with the stage name Robin Daggers, she moved to New York City and became a news anchor, eventually hosting her own early-morning talk show.

relationships.Ted Mosby: Robin's on-and-off love interest and close friend. They date at the end of season one but break up at the end of season two. Despite this, they remain close friends and have lingering romantic feelings for each other. In the series finale, it is revealed that Robin and Barney divorced, and Robin and Ted were in a relationship in the broadcast ending.
relationships.Marshall Eriksen: A close friend and colleague. Marshall is part of Robin's tight-knit group of friends in New York City.
relationships.Barney Stinson: Robin's husband (married in 2013, divorced in 2016 according to the broadcast ending). Their relationship becomes romantic in the eighth season, leading to Barney's elaborate ruse to win Robin back and their subsequent marriage. They have a strong bond, but their marriage faces challenges.
relationships.Lily Aldrin: A close friend and colleague. Lily is part of Robin's tight-knit group of friends in New York City and is supportive of Robin throughout the series.

personality: Independent, career-driven, and initially reluctant to settle down. Robin is known for her sarcasm, wit, and a strong sense of self. She is also a loyal friend and has a deep-seated aversion to shopping malls due to her past as a teen pop star. Despite her tough exterior, she is capable of vulnerability, especially when it comes to her inability to have children and her romantic relationships.
style_guide: Robin often uses sarcasm and quick, witty remarks. She is known for her catchphrase 'Suit up!' and her tendency to refer to herself as 'Aunt Robin' when talking to Ted's children.
